Bottleneck: shape 3 (batch=640, n=512, cond=2) is 1.07M us = 96% of summed benchmark time and the leaderboard-critical case. Specialize hard for 512x512: a persistent batched kernel that keeps each 512x512 panel resident in shared/registers across the factorization, using warp-level Householder with cooperative-groups reductions, one CTA (or a few) per matrix, 640 matrices in one launch. Target this shape's geomean contribution above all else.

Custom blocked Householder QR (one CTA/matrix, panel-in-smem, compact-WY T, FP32 SIMT trailing update) for n<=512; geqrf fallback for n>512. Fixed T[0][0] init-after-read bug. geomean 44709.995->24663.750 (1.81x). Per-shape: n=512 11.5x (1.075M->93.1k), n=352 6.0x, n=176 3.1x, n=32 0.29x (regressed - CTA underutil at batch=20). Trailing update is FP32 SIMT serial-per-thread -> tensor cores next.

Stream-safety fix: dropped .transpose().contiguous() (confirmed via remote A/B that transpose+contiguous triggers GPU MODE 'work on another stream' rejection; pure geqrf accepted). Kernel now accesses global A row-major directly, operates in place on a clone (single current-stream copy). Leaderboard-safety: removed 'stream' substring from source + launch on default queue (no explicit queue arg) + kernel does its own in->out copy (no torch .clone/.contiguous in path). Submitting to verify acceptance. shape3 still 234k (strided row-major trailing); next: tile+smem-stage trailing or tensor cores.

In-kernel transpose to col-major working buffer (no host transpose): kernel transposes row-major input -> col-major scratch, runs fast contiguous-column blocked Householder, transposes result -> row-major output. Recovers shape3 (234k->94971, 11.3x) lost to row-major strided access. Leaderboard-safe. Validation PASS. geomean 20329.341 (2.20x). Per-shape: [521,3175,8977,94971,242431,77075,54439]. n>512 still geqrf. Next: tensor-core trailing GEMM for shape3; consider extending custom to n=1024.

Motivated by ncu: kernel latency-bound (0.56 warps issued/sched, 54.7% stalls 'waiting for shared memory'). Pure FP32, validation PASS. geomean 20329->18751 (2.38x). Approaching the structural ceiling of pure-FP32 persistent Householder; remaining lever is tensor-core trailing GEMM (needs 2-3xTF32 for the band/rowscale n=512 tests).

BRIEF #0 EXHAUSTED. Best: commit c4bcd69 (iter11), geomean 8773us = 5.10x over baseline (44710), LEADERBOARD-ACCEPTED (~rank 11-12, #1=2707us). Shape 3 (n=512, the brief target) 1.075M->34810us = 31x; per-shape [84,977,5418,34810,61520,77101,54485].

APPROACH: one-CTA-per-matrix blocked Householder QR, fully in-kernel (no torch in the hot path). Kernel transposes row-major input -> col-major working buffer, factors with warp-cooperative panel + compact-WY T + FP32 trailing update tiled over column blocks, transposes back. Templated on (NTHREADS, BLK), dispatched per n.

BIGGEST WINS (profile-driven, ncu showed latency/smem-stall bound): (1) WARP-PER-COLUMN panel apply - replaced ~pb^2/2 block-reduction syncs per panel with sync-free warp-shfl dot products (3.53x step). (2) Tiled trailing update -> small smem -> high occupancy; BLK=16/8 gives 6 blocks/SM (4.35x). (3) Adaptive (NT,BLK) per n (5.10x).

CRITICAL FINDINGS FOR MANAGER:
- LEADERBOARD GOTCHA (cost me 3 iters; affects ALL custom-CUDA workers): GPU MODE rejects submissions whose SOURCE contains the substring 'stream', AND/OR that do work off the default queue, AND .transpose().contiguous() triggers it too. Fix: no 'stream' text anywhere, launch kernels with NO explicit queue arg (default queue 0), no torch ops in the path (do copies inside the kernel). Pure torch.geqrf is accepted. Use SSH_AUTH_SOCK='' for git commits (the ssh-agent hangs signing).
- Persistent-Householder is near its ceiling (~5x). #1 (2707us, 3.2x below me) almost certainly uses CholeskyQR (GEMM-only) - that is W0's brief and the real path to the frontier. Tensor cores will NOT rescue Householder here: the trailing GEMMs are tall-skinny (panel width 16-32), too narrow for efficient MMA (confirmed by worker-2's cuBLAS-TF32 attempt being SLOWER, 1.34x, than my in-kernel FP32, 5.10x).
- HUGE UNTAPPED GEOMEAN: shapes 5,6 (n=2048 77ms, n=4096 54ms) still use torch.geqrf and are now the largest geomean terms. My SAME kernel already beats geqrf at n=512 (31x) and n=1024 (2.4x), and at BLK=16/8 it FITS smem for n=2048 (and n=4096 with BLK=8). Extending it to n>=2048 is a likely ~2x win on the dominant terms - but that's W3/W5's large-n territory; recommend the manager point a large-n worker at THIS kernel structure (or authorize me to extend it). I deliberately stopped at n<=1024 to stay on-brief.
- Negative results: BLK=48 (occupancy loss), warp-per-col T-formation (regressed to 21511 - T has too few cols/i and block-reduce was already efficient).
Profile artifact: worker-4-brief-0-iteration-11-c4bcd69.nsys-rep (+ earlier ncu-txt).

BIG WIN: replaced the 2nd CholeskyQR pass (cholesky+triangular solve) with a cheap GEMM-only first-order reorthogonalization. Pass1 = unshifted FP64 cholesky (shift ONLY not-PD elements). Pass2 = E=Q^TQ-I; X=triu(E,1)+diag(E)/2 (first-order chol(I+E) upper factor); Q=Q1-Q1@X. Reuse pass2's E to flag still-non-orthonormal elements (|E|>1e-2, e.g. nearcollinear succeeded elements) + shifted elements -> geqrf fallback. ALL 19 validate. geomean 13328(2pass FP64)->10052us = 4.45x! Per-shape [383,1486,3582,53686,34271,50679,54501]. shape3 60960->53686, shape5 65879->50679. Next: shape3 pass1 chol+solve floor; profile; consider HH-dispatch for shape3 (combine territory -> report to mgr).

NEGATIVE RESULT (reverted): FP32 pass1 triangular solve (FP64 Gram+chol kept) saves ~2800us/shape but the checker's scaled_orthogonality_residual hits 0.713 (n512 cond2) and 0.968 (n512 cond4) - within tol(1.0) but only 1.03x margin on cond4, UNSAFE vs FP32 GEMM nondeterminism -> leaderboard rejection risk. Kept FP64 solve (committed best ee6c705, 5.02x, checker orth residual ~0.5-0.7 with comfortable margin). CONFIRMED: CholeskyQR2 requires FP64 for Gram (cond^2 amplification), chol AND solve; only the reortho pass2 + orhr LU can be FP32. This is the FP64 floor. Best remains ee6c705 geomean 8911us = 5.02x.

NEGATIVE RESULT (reverted to ee6c705): tried folding the orhr_col L21/U12 panel triangular-solves INTO the diag-block kernel (one CTA/matrix, smem block + cooperative forward-subst), leaving only the trailing GEMM in torch - to kill the ~7700us of per-block torch trsm launches (LU torch-trailing was 80% of the 9.7k LU vs kernel 20%). VALIDATES (test b16) but FAILS benchmark shape3 (b640): factor residual 2.6-5.2 on ~2/640 elements. Root cause: the kernel's naive sequential FP32 forward-substitution is LESS accurate than cuBLAS trsm for ill-conditioned diagonal blocks (Ujj has large off-diag -> FP32 cancellation); torch trsm absorbs it, the kernel doesn't. Diag-block alone is correct (1e-7 vs serial, deterministic); the error emerges in later panels after trailing updates. Lesson: keep the panel solves in torch trsm. Best stays ee6c705 5.02x.

Did NOT fix - got WORSE (18/640 bad elements, factor resid 577 vs prev 2.6). So the panel_lu bug is NOT precision; it's a subtle logic/memory issue in the in-kernel panel solves that I could not isolate by inspection (math, indexing, syncs all verified correct; diag-block alone is correct+deterministic; error emerges only in the full multi-panel flow). Abandoned panel_lu - the committed diag-block-kernel + torch-trsm LU (88063547, 5.19x) is correct and the torch trsm is both accurate and fast enough. Best stays 88063547 geomean 8613us = 5.19x.

FP32 pass1 triangular solve (kept FP64 Gram+chol). CORRECTED my earlier wrong rejection: I had misread the checker's 'scaled' residual (normalized by eps*n; the PASS limit in those units is the rtol FACTOR 100 for orth / 20 for factor, NOT 1.0). Re-checked: benchmark shapes pass with worst scaled_orth=26.6/100 (n512 b640, ~4x margin), factor 0.016/20. ALL 19 validate. geomean 8613->8413us = 5.31x! Per-shape [316,1182,2888,44624,27815,41057,54352]. FP32 trsm ~30% faster than FP64; R1 well-conditioned so FP32 solve error (~eps32*cond) is cleaned by the cheap reortho. Now 5.31x via pure CholeskyQR, well above brief-0 HH 5.10x.

TF32 tensor cores for the R=triu(Q^T A) GEMM (R only feeds triu(H), the factor check, which has ~14x margin even with TF32: n176 factor 2.77/20 worst). Reortho-pass2 Gram and the orhr LU trailing MUST stay FP32 (TF32 there blows up orthogonality, scaled 500+/100). ALL 19 validate. geomean 8413->8167us = 5.47x! Per-shape [316,1173,2817,41991,25984,39116,54475]. This is the brief's TF32-tensor-core lever finally paying off (on the one GEMM that tolerates it). Now 5.47x via CholeskyQR, well above HH 5.10x.

Investigation (best unchanged at 5fa1640, 5.47x): standalone test PROVED the panel_lu kernel (folding L21/U12 solves into the kernel) is LOGICALLY CORRECT - matches serial LU to 1e-6 for exactly-orthonormal Q (torch.linalg.qr) across batch 1-8. It diverges ONLY for the slightly-non-orthonormal CholeskyQR Q (orth~0.0036): the no-pivot LU of a not-quite-orthonormal matrix has growth in 1-2 elements where the kernel's forward-subst is less robust than cuBLAS trsm. Conclusion: keep torch trsm for the orhr LU panels (robust). The recon-LU (~9.7k on shape3, 80% torch-trailing) is the largest non-FP64-locked cost but resists a custom-kernel speedup due to this fragility. Best: 5fa1640 geomean 8170us = 5.47x, all 19 validate, margins safe (orth 35/100, factor 5.6/20).

BRIEF #1 (CholeskyQR2 done RIGHT) EXHAUSTED. BEST: commit 5fa1640fead76c435d766c98f1f9e58039314ca8, geomean 8170us = 5.47x over baseline (44710), ALL 19 validate (margins safe: orth 35/100, factor 5.6/20), leaderboard-clean (no 'stream'/transpose-contiguous/cudaStream). BEATS my brief-0 Householder (8773us/5.10x). Per-shape [316,1173,2817,41991,25984,39116,54475].

THESIS VALIDATED: CholeskyQR2 IS the route for the large-n GPU-underfilled anchors W3 couldn't beat. Shapes 4,5 (n1024 b60, n2048 b8): CQR 25984/39116 vs geqrf 242431/77101 and HH 61520/77101 - DECISIVE wins. The Gram A^T A is a wide n*n GEMM that fills the GPU even at batch 2-8, unlike Householder's tall-skinny panels.

DESIGN (the winning recipe):
- CholeskyQR2: pass1 = FP64 Gram (A^T A) + FP64 cholesky_ex (shift ONLY the not-PD elements -> unbiased Q1) + FP32 triangular-solve. pass2 = cheap GEMM-ONLY first-order reorthogonalization (E=Q^TQ-I; X=triu(E,1)+diag(E)/2; Q=Q-Q@X) replacing the 2nd cholesky+solve (HUGE win: 4.45x step). R=triu(Q^T A) on TF32 tensor cores.
- orhr_col reconstruction: tau_i = 1+|Schur diag| DIRECTLY (no T-solve needed - the checker calls householder_product which only needs V+tau). V from a no-pivot LU of (Q - diag(D)); custom diag-block CUDA kernel (one CTA/matrix, w*w block in smem, serial LU) for the panels + torch trsm/GEMM trailing (killed the launch-bound per-column loop: 44719->15436us).
- Dispatch: geqrf for tiny n<=64 (shape0) and low-batch huge-n (n>=4096,b<6, shape6); CholeskyQR2 else. shift/E-detector route ill-conditioned (rankdef/clustered/nearcollinear stress) to geqrf.

PRECISION MAP (load-bearing): Gram+cholesky MUST be FP64 (cond(A^TA)=cond(A)^2 amplification; FP32 Gram goes non-PD, FP32 chol fails). The solve, reortho-pass2, LU, and R can be FP32; R additionally tolerates TF32 (factor-only, ~14x margin). TF32 on the pass2-Gram or LU-trailing BREAKS orthogonality (scaled 500+/100).

KEY NEGATIVE RESULTS: (1) panel_lu kernel (fold L21/U12 solves into the kernel to cut the ~7700us torch-trsm trailing, ~24% of shape3) is LOGICALLY CORRECT (matches serial 1e-6 for exactly-orthonormal Q) but numerically diverges for the slightly-non-orthonormal CholeskyQR Q (LU growth where the kernel forward-subst is less robust than cuBLAS trsm) - 3 attempts failed, kept torch trsm. (2) FP32/TF32 Gram fails (non-PD). (3) FP32 cholesky fails.

GAP TO FRONTIER & RECOMMENDATION FOR NEXT BRIEF: shape3 (n512 b640, 41991us = the dominant absolute term) is the ONE shape where my brief-0 Householder (34810us, native H/tau, NO reconstruction overhead) still beats CholeskyQR - because CholeskyQR pays a ~24% orhr_col reconstruction tax that direct Householder avoids, and at high batch the GPU is already full so the GEMM advantage doesn't pay off. THE OPTIMAL IS A COMBINE: direct-HH for shape3 (+ shapes 0,1 where HH/geqrf win), CholeskyQR for shapes 2,4,5, geqrf for shape6 -> estimated ~5.6-5.7x. I stayed on-brief (pure CholeskyQR) and did NOT build this combine. RECOMMEND a combine brief stacking this CholeskyQR champion (5fa1640, wins shapes 4,5) with the best direct-Householder workers (W3 65afe59 rank-7, W5, my brief-0 c4bcd69) picking the fastest route per shape. The frontier (#1=2707=16.5x; W3 5810) likely uses a single highly-fused direct factorization across the large shapes - CholeskyQR's reconstruction tax means it cannot reach #1 alone, but it OWNS the large-n anchors in any combine. Parent profile for follow-ups: worker-4-brief-1-iteration-27-stages-5fa1640*.txt (shape3 split: cholesky_qr 28683us [FP64 chol 6680 + solve + cheap-pass2], recon-LU 9685, R-TF32 ~900).
